title: Twist-unlock a new lotion bottle's pump and turn its spout to you, with no squirt
instruction: The pump on the new lotion bottle is locked down. Twist the head to unlock it so it springs up, then turn the spout to point at you (-x). Do not press the head down once it is up and do not tip the bottle.
context: Body lotion, liquid soap and shampoo pump bottles come with the pump head locked down for shipping; nearly everyone has twisted one until it pops up. The bottle stands on a non-slip shelf liner in front of a tiled splash wall, as on a bathroom vanity. The head rides on a spring: once the quarter turn frees it, it rises by itself, and any downward push while it is gripped and turned starts a stroke and squirts lotion over the hand, the liner or the tiles. The spout is then swung round to face the user, so the first press lands in the palm and not on the wall. Done means the head up, the spout to the front, the bottle where it was and nothing pumped; the first dose is left to the user.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). Three objects; one gripper is enough (the right one reaches the bottle). (1) Shelf liner, fixed: a 220 x 220 x 3 mm sheet of dark grey rubber (non-slip, friction 1.0, est), centred at (0.280, -0.250). (2) Splash wall, fixed: white glazed tile on a board, 20 mm thick, 300 mm tall, x 0.430 to 0.450, y -0.620 to -0.020 (150 mm behind the bottle's axis). (3) Lotion bottle, loose, standing on the liner at (0.280, -0.250): a 12 fl oz (355 ml) round white HDPE bottle 66 mm across, 107 mm to its shoulder, with a 24/410 closure (33 mm across, 15 mm tall) and a black polypropylene lock-down pump; full, 0.42 kg in all (a rigid mass: no liquid is modelled), 148 mm tall with the head locked, base friction 0.8 (est). Pump head: a ribbed cap 32 mm across and 26 mm tall with a spout 9 mm across running out sideways from its top to 48 mm from the bottle's axis, its nozzle pointing down. Locked, the head sits down on the closure (top 148 mm up, a bayonet with two lugs holds it); a quarter turn anticlockwise (seen from above) frees the lugs, which clear at 80 degrees, and the pump spring lifts the head 23 mm to its top position (top 171 mm up). The turn takes about 0.035 N m at the lugs (est). Free, the head swivels either way with about 0.01 N m of friction (est) and stands on its spring, 1.6 N for the first 4 mm of push (est); pushed more than 4 mm down it starts a stroke. Start: head locked, spout pointing -y; after the unlocking turn it points +x, away from the robot. The bottle on the liner resists about 0.08 N m of twist (est), more than the lock takes, so it stays put while the head is turned. Nothing else is on the table. Real build: a new 12 fl oz HDPE Boston-round bottle with a 24/410 lock-down lotion pump from a packaging supplier, with the dip tube cut off and a sealed bag of dry sand inside to 0.42 kg, so a stroke pumps only air and nothing needs cleaning; a rubber shelf liner; a 300 mm tile or board as the wall.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the bottle's pose, the pump head's height and turn, and both grippers; the stroke and tip gates are read at every step. Standing: the bottle upright (tilt under 8 degrees) with its base centre within 30 mm of its start (top view). Unlocked: the head has been turned 80 degrees or more at some moment and now stands 18 mm or more above its locked height. Spout: the spout's direction within 15 degrees of -x in top view. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from every part of the bottle, and over that 1 s the bottle moves under 5 mm and turns under 5 degrees and the head turns under 5 degrees and moves under 5 mm. Score 0 if at any time the bottle tips more than 45 degrees or falls off the vanity (its base 50 mm below its start height), or the head, once free, is pushed more than 4 mm below the highest it has been (a stroke: lotion pumped out), and 0 unless standing and hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 unlocked with the spout to the front; 0.5 unlocked, spout elsewhere; 0.25 not unlocked but the head was turned 30 degrees or more toward unlocking at some moment; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Which way the spout was swung is not scored. Doing nothing scores 0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: standing, an 8 degree angle gauge and a ring template on the liner for the 30 mm; unlocked, a rule from the closure's top to the head's top (18 mm more than locked) and the video for the turn; spout, a protractor on the table under the spout against a line along -x through the bottle's start mark; stroke, 60 fps side video of the head against a rule (4 mm); hands off, a 30 mm spacer block and 30 fps video of the last 1 s; tip gate, by eye. A fresh bottle, or the same one pressed down and re-locked, is used per trial.
fidelity: Rigid bottle (lotion as fixed mass). The bayonet is declared: a torsion spring (0.025 N m/rad) stands for the lock's turning torque until the head has turned 80 degrees (a head let go earlier springs back; a real one stays put), then the lugs are clear and the pump spring (400 N/m) lifts the head; free swivel is joint damping. A stroke is scored, not simulated as liquid. Frictions are estimates.
reset_notes: Turn the spout to point -y, press the head down to the closure and turn it a quarter turn clockwise (seen from above) until it locks. Stand the bottle on its mark at (0.280, -0.250) on the liner. The sand-ballasted dry bottle consumes nothing; a stroke only moves air.
